+-- | Jobs gathered into their runs, newest run first. A run's jobs come in
+-- the order the run made them, which is how its pages number them.
+runsOf :: [Api.Task] -> [C.Run]
+runsOf tasks =
+  [ C.Run
+      { number = n
+      , workflow = t.workflowId
+      , title = t.displayTitle
+      , branch = t.headBranch
+      , event = t.event
+      , sha = t.headSha
+      , state = overall (map (.state) jobs)
+      , started = minimum (map (.startedAt) ts)
+      , updated = maximum (map (.updatedAt) ts)
+      , url = t.url
+      , jobs = jobs
+      }
+  | ts@(t : _) <- map (sortOn (.id)) (sortOn (Down . maximum . map (.id)) (Map.elems byRun))
+  , Just n <- [readMaybe (T.unpack (T.takeWhileEnd (/= '/') t.url))]
+  , let jobs = zipWith (jobCheck n) [0 ..] ts
+  ]
+  where
+    byRun = Map.fromListWith (flip (<>)) [(t.url, [t]) | t <- tasks]
+    jobCheck n i t = C.Check
+      { name = t.name
+      , state = taskState t.status
+      , description = case taskState t.status of
+          C.Running -> "Running"
+          C.Waiting -> "Waiting"
+          C.Skipped -> "Skipped"
+          _ -> "Took " <> took (diffUTCTime t.updatedAt t.startedAt)
+      , url = Just (t.url <> "/jobs/" <> T.pack (show i))
+      , job = Just C.Job {run = n, index = i}
+      }
+    took d = let s = round d :: Int in
+      if s < 60 then T.pack (show s) <> "s" else T.pack (show (s `div` 60)) <> "m " <> T.pack (show (s `mod` 60)) <> "s"
+    taskState s = case s of
+      "success" -> C.Passed
+      "failure" -> C.Failed
+      "cancelled" -> C.Failed
+      "skipped" -> C.Skipped
+      "running" -> C.Running
+      _ -> C.Waiting
+    overall states
+      | C.Failed `elem` states = C.Failed
+      | C.Running `elem` states = C.Running
+      | C.Waiting `elem` states = C.Waiting
+      | all (== C.Skipped) states = C.Skipped
+      | otherwise = C.Passed
+
 -- | The job a status links, "…/actions/runs/{run}/jobs/{index}".
 jobOf :: Text -> Maybe C.Job
 jobOf u = case reverse (T.splitOn "/" u) of

and only what was sent is taken off it.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/test/Usta/LocalFilesTests.hs
@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+{-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
+
+-- | What usta keeps beside its cache: drafts, viewed files, actions
+-- waiting for the forge, pins, the log, and tokens in a keyring. The
+-- tests' own home holds them (see Main).
+module Usta.LocalFilesTests (tests) where
+
+import Control.Concurrent (forkIO)
+import Control.Concurrent.MVar (newEmptyMVar, putMVar, takeMVar)
+import Control.Monad (forM_)
+import qualified Data.Map.Strict as Map
+import qualified Data.Text as T
+import System.Directory (getHomeDirectory)
+import Test.Tasty (DependencyType (..), TestTree, sequentialTestGroup)
+import Test.Tasty.HUnit (assertBool, testCase, (@?=))
+
+import qualified Usta.Drafts as Drafts
+import qualified Usta.Keyring as Keyring
+import qualified Usta.Log as Log
+import qualified Usta.Pins as Pins
+import Usta.Types.Parse (parseM, unparse)
+import Usta.Types.Token (Token)
+import qualified Usta.Viewed as Viewed
+import Usta.Waiting (Action (..))
+import qualified Usta.Waiting as Waiting
+
+tests :: TestTree
+tests =
+  -- One after another: they share the files and the log.
+  sequentialTestGroup
+    "Local files"
+    AllFinish
+    [ testCase "a draft is kept, and an empty one taken away" $ do
+        Drafts.keep "github.com/a/b#1" "half a comment"
+        Drafts.load "github.com/a/b#1" >>= (@?= "half a comment")
+        Drafts.keep "github.com/a/b#1" "  \n"
+        Drafts.load "github.com/a/b#1" >>= (@?= "")
+    , testCase "drafts are kept by where they were written" $ do
+        Drafts.keep "x#1" "one"
+        Drafts.keep "x#2" "two"
+        (,) <$> Drafts.load "x#1" <*> Drafts.load "x#2" >>= (@?= ("one", "two"))
+    , testCase "viewed files" $ do
+        Viewed.keep "pr" (Map.fromList [("src/A.hs", "abc")])
+        Viewed.load "pr" >>= (@?= Map.fromList [("src/A.hs", "abc")])
+        Viewed.keep "pr" Map.empty
+        Viewed.load "pr" >>= (@?= Map.empty)
+    , testCase "actions wait in order" $ do
+        Waiting.update (const [])
+        Waiting.add Comment {host = "github.com", repo = "a/usta", number = 3, text = "hi"}
+        Waiting.add Done {host = "github.com", repo = "a/usta", number = 4}
+        map Waiting.describe <$> Waiting.load >>= (@?= ["Comment on usta #3", "Mark usta #4 done"])
+        Waiting.update (const [])
+        Waiting.load >>= (@?= [])
+    , testCase "actions added at once are all kept" $ do
+        Waiting.update (const [])
+        done <- newEmptyMVar
+        forM_ [1 .. 40] $ \n -> forkIO (Waiting.add Done {host = "github.com", repo = "a/usta", number = n} >> putMVar done ())
+        forM_ [1 .. 40 :: Int] $ \_ -> takeMVar done
+        length <$> Waiting.load >>= (@?= 40)
+        Waiting.update (const [])
+    , testCase "one send of what waits at a time" $ do
+        Waiting.update (const [Done {host = "github.com", repo = "a/usta", number = 1}])
+        started <- newEmptyMVar
+        finish <- newEmptyMVar
+        first <- newEmptyMVar
+        _ <- forkIO (Waiting.sending (putMVar started () >> takeMVar finish >> pure 0) >>= putMVar first)
+        takeMVar started
+        second <- Waiting.sending (pure 99)
+        putMVar finish ()
+        (,) second <$> takeMVar first >>= (@?= (1, 0))
+        Waiting.update (const [])
+    , testCase "pins, once each, in the order pinned" $ do
+        Pins.setPinned ("github.com", "a/one") True
+        Pins.setPinned ("github.com", "a/two") True
+        Pins.setPinned ("github.com", "a/one") True
+        Pins.pins >>= (@?= [("github.com", "a/two"), ("github.com", "a/one")])
+        Pins.setPinned ("github.com", "a/two") False
+        Pins.pins >>= (@?= [("github.com", "a/one")])
+    , testCase "the log writes the home folder as ~" $ do
+        home <- T.pack <$> getHomeDirectory
+        Log.say "test" ("opened " <> home <> "/x.txt")
+        found <- Log.lastLines 1
+        assertBool (show found) (any ("opened ~/x.txt" `T.isInfixOf`) found && not (any (home `T.isInfixOf`) found))
+    , testCase "a message of many lines stays one entry" $ do
+        Log.say "test" "first\nsecond"
+        found <- Log.lastLines 2
+        map (T.isSuffixOf "test  first") (take 1 found) <> map (== "         second") (drop 1 found) @?= [True, True]
+    , testCase "a crash is told at the next start" $ do
+        _ <- Log.start
+        crashed <- Log.start
+        Log.stop
+        clean <- Log.start
+        Log.stop
+        (crashed, clean) @?= (True, False)
+    , testCase "the memory keyring" $ do
+        keyring <- Keyring.memory
+        host <- parseM "github.com"
+        login <- parseM "a"
+        other <- parseM "b"
+        token <- parseM "ghp_secret" :: IO Token
+        keyring.save host login token
+        fmap unparse <$> keyring.load host login >>= (@?= Just "ghp_secret")
+        fmap unparse <$> keyring.load host other >>= (@?= Nothing)
+        keyring.forget host login
+        fmap unparse <$> keyring.load host login >>= (@?= Nothing)
+    ]

# usta

[![Landing page](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/actions/workflows/pages/pages-build-deployment/badge.svg)](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/actions/workflows/pages/pages-build-deployment)

A desktop client to connect with your forge.

usta shows your pull requests, issues and notifications from GitHub and
Forgejo in one fast native window, for macOS and Linux. It is written in
Haskell with GTK 4. See it at <https://usta.azizovich.uz>.

**usta is in beta** (0.1.0). GitHub and Forgejo work end to end: the
inbox, pull request reviews on local git diffs, checks and workflows,
issues, repositories, and an offline cache. GitLab comes next. What is in
each release is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md); the design lives in
[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Install

Each [release](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/releases) has
`usta.dmg` for macOS, and `usta-x86_64.AppImage`, a `.deb` and an `.rpm`
for Linux. The macOS app is not signed by Apple yet: the first time,
open it with right-click › Open, or allow it in System Settings › Privacy
& Security.

Installed, usta opens `usta://<forge link>` links, such as
`usta://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/1`, from anywhere on the
system. Once a day it checks for a newer release (Settings > Updates).

### With Nix

The flake has a Home Manager module, for macOS and Linux, and NixOS and
nix-darwin modules. On macOS they install `usta.app` (Home Manager links
it into `~/Applications/Home Manager Apps`), so `usta://` links and
notifications work.

```nix
{
  inputs.usta.url = "github:abdivasiyev/usta";

  # in a Home Manager configuration
  imports = [ inputs.usta.homeManagerModules.default ];
  programs.usta = {
    enable = true;
    settings = {
      interval = "5m";        # "1m", "2m", "5m", "15m" or "manual"
      theme = "dark";         # "system", "light" or "dark"
      notifications = true;
      onlyInBackground = false;
      openLinks = true;
      checkUpdates = false;
    };
  };
}
```

Each setting is optional. One that is set shows as "Set in Nix" in
usta's Settings and is not changed there; the rest stay yours. Home
Manager writes them to `~/.config/usta/config.json`.
`nixosModules.default` and `darwinModules.default` take the same
`programs.usta` options for every user, written to
`/etc/xdg/usta/config.json`; a user's own Home Manager settings win
over them. `overlays.default` adds `pkgs.usta`.

## Run

With [Nix](https://nixos.org) and flakes enabled:

```sh
nix run github:abdivasiyev/usta
```

## Build

Everything comes from the flake: GHC 9.12, GTK 4 and the Haskell
dependencies.

```sh
nix build        # the app, in ./result/bin/usta
nix develop      # a shell with GHC, cabal and haskell-language-server
```

Inside `nix develop`:

```sh
cabal build
cabal run usta
```

`cabal run usta -- <flag>` opens other screens, for working on them:

| Flag           | Opens                                    |
|----------------|------------------------------------------|
| `--gallery`    | every component on one page              |
| `--welcome`    | the first-run screen, before any account |
| `--first-sync` | the inbox while the first sync runs      |

## Release

`scripts/macos-app.sh` builds `dist/usta.app` and `dist/usta.dmg` with
every library inside, so they run without Nix; set `USTA_SIGN_IDENTITY`
to sign with a Developer ID. Pushing a tag `v<version>` that matches
`usta.cabal` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds both
downloads and attaches them to a new release; its header lists the
secrets for signing and notarizing.

## Contributing

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setting up, testing and pull
requests, and [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for how the
code is built. The landing page is <https://usta.azizovich.uz>.

The Releases tab of a GitHub repository shows:

> The forge said: the forge sent an answer usta cannot read

It happens on `abdivasiyev/usta` since `v0.1.0`, whose release was created by the release workflow.

## Why

GitHub lists that release's author as `github-actions[bot]`. `Usta.Types.Login` accepts only letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` (`isPathSegment`), so the brackets of a bot account fail the parse, and with it the whole list of releases.

The same parse runs on every author and login usta reads from GitHub, so anything a bot wrote can fail the same way: Dependabot or Renovate pull requests, CI bot comments, reviews by bots.

## Fix

Let `Login` take GitHub's bot accounts (`<name>[bot]`), while still refusing anything that is not a user name; and check the pull request, issue and comment lists with a bot author.

# A tag v<version> builds the release: usta.dmg on macOS, and on Linux
# usta-x86_64.AppImage, a .deb and an .rpm, attached to a GitHub release with
# generated notes. The tag must match usta.cabal's version, which is the
# version the update check compares.
#
# Signing on macOS needs these secrets; without them the app is signed ad
# hoc and Gatekeeper asks before it opens:
#   MACOS_CERTIFICATE           base64 of a Developer ID Application .p12
#   MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD  its password
#   MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY         e.g. "Developer ID Application: Name (TEAMID)"
#   APPLE_ID, APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_APP_PASSWORD   for notarization
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: The tag matches usta.cabal
        run: |
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version: *//p' usta.cabal)
          if [ "v$version" != "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" ]; then
            echo "Tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME, but usta.cabal says $version" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Create the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          version=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}
          # Before 1.0 a release is a beta, said in its title; it stays a
          # regular release, since "latest" leaves pre-releases out and the
          # downloads and the update check go by it.
          title="usta $version"
          case "$version" in 0.*) title="$title (beta)";; esac
          # The notes are the version's part of CHANGELOG.md.
          awk -v v="$version" '/^## / {on = index($0, "## " v) == 1; next} on' CHANGELOG.md > notes.md
          if [ -s notes.md ]; then
            gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --title "$title" --notes-file notes.md
          else
            gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --title "$title" --generate-notes
          fi

  macos:
    needs: release
    runs-on: macos-14
    env:
      SIGNING: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE != '' }}
      NOTARIZING: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID != '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@v16
      - name: Import the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGNING == 'true'
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          keychain=$RUNNER_TEMP/usta.keychain-db
          echo "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE" | base64 --decode > "$RUNNER_TEMP/usta.p12"
          security create-keychain -p usta "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 3600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p usta "$keychain"
          security import "$RUNNER_TEMP/usta.p12" -k "$keychain" -P "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD" -T /usr/bin/codesign
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -k usta "$keychain"
          security list-keychains -d user -s "$keychain"
      - name: Build usta.app and usta.dmg
        env:
          USTA_SIGN_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.MACOS_SIGN_IDENTITY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$USTA_SIGN_IDENTITY" ]; then unset USTA_SIGN_IDENTITY; fi
          ./scripts/macos-app.sh dist
      - name: Notarize
        if: env.NOTARIZING == 'true'
        env:
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          xcrun notarytool submit dist/usta.dmg --apple-id "$APPLE_ID" --team-id "$APPLE_TEAM_ID" --password "$APPLE_APP_PASSWORD" --wait
          xcrun stapler staple dist/usta.dmg
      - name: Attach to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" dist/usta.dmg --clobber

  linux:
    needs: release
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      # GHC 9.12's packages are not in the binary cache, so nix builds
      # them, gi-gtk4 with its docs among them: the runner's 14 GB run
      # out. The SDKs it carries and usta does not use free 30 more.
      - name: Make room on the disk
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost
          sudo docker image prune --all --force
          df -h /
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@v16
      - name: Build the AppImage, .deb and .rpm
        # The .deb and .rpm carry usta's own GTK under /nix/store: the
        # distributions' GTK is older than the 4.20 usta needs.
        run: |
          nix bundle --bundler github:ralismark/nix-appimage .#usta -o usta.AppImage
          cp -L usta.AppImage usta-x86_64.AppImage
          nix bundle --bundler github:NixOS/bundlers#toDEB .#usta -o deb
          cp -L deb/*.deb "usta_${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}_amd64.deb"
          nix bundle --bundler github:NixOS/bundlers#toRPM .#usta -o rpm
          cp -L rpm/*.rpm "usta-${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}.x86_64.rpm"
      - name: Attach to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: gh release upload "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" usta-x86_64.AppImage ./*.deb ./*.rpm --clobber

The first release of usta: a native desktop client for GitHub and Forgejo,
for macOS and Linux. It is a beta: things will change, and some parts are
still missing (see Not yet, below).

### Inbox and notifications

- One inbox for review requests, mentions, assignments and failed checks,
  across every forge you sign in to; mark done, all at once, or move back.
- Desktop notifications for what needs you, also while usta is in front.
- Pull request and issue lists with tabs, filters by forge, repository,
  label and author, sorting, and the forge's counts.

### Pull requests

- The conversation in one live timeline: comments, reviews, commits and
  events, with replies on Enter, reactions, editing and drafts that stay.
- Reviews on real git diffs from a local mirror, or the forge's API: split
  or unified, whitespace hidden, changed words marked, more context on
  demand, and comments on a line or a range.
- The file's header stays at the top of a long diff, and files you viewed
  stay viewed until they change.
- Reviewers, assignees, labels and milestones; merge, squash or rebase,
  auto-merge, update the branch, draft and ready.
- Checks with live job logs in color, folded groups and steps; run a
  workflow with its inputs, re-run failed jobs or cancel a run (GitHub).
- New pull requests, also from a fork; check out a pull request locally.

### Repositories

- Every repository you can see, filtered by forge and owner, and any other
  repository a link or a search opens.
- Files with type icons, syntax colors, blame and history; README and
  Markdown with Mermaid diagrams drawn natively.
- Commits, releases, insights and the repository's actions.
- Fork, clone, star, pin, mirror, and create new repositories.

### Everywhere

- ⌘K / Ctrl K searches pull requests, issues and repositories on every
  forge, and runs commands; links you paste open their page.
- Keyboard first: j and k, Enter, e; Emacs keys in every text field.
- Works offline from its cache, and syncs in the background.
- usta can be the default browser on macOS: forge links from any app open
  in usta, every other link goes on to the browser you choose.
- Light and dark themes; settings can be set from Nix (Home Manager,
  NixOS, nix-darwin).
- Sign in with a token (GitHub, Forgejo) or in the browser (Forgejo);
  tokens stay in the system keyring.
- A daily check for a newer release, and Report a problem with the log.

### Not yet

- GitLab.
- Signing in to GitHub in the browser; tokens work.
- A signed macOS app: macOS asks once before opening it.
- Forgejo review texts in the conversation, and re-running or cancelling
  Forgejo Actions runs (Forgejo has no API for them).

# usta

[![Landing page](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/actions/workflows/pages/pages-build-deployment/badge.svg)](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/actions/workflows/pages/pages-build-deployment)

A desktop client to connect with your forge.

usta shows your pull requests, issues and notifications from GitHub and
Forgejo in one fast native window, for macOS and Linux. It is written in
Haskell with GTK 4. See it at <https://usta.azizovich.uz>.

**usta is in beta** (0.1.0). GitHub and Forgejo work end to end: the
inbox, pull request reviews on local git diffs, checks and workflows,
issues, repositories, and an offline cache. GitLab comes next. What is in
each release is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md); the design lives in
[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Install

Each [release](https://github.com/abdivasiyev/usta/releases) has
`usta.dmg` for macOS, and `usta-x86_64.AppImage`, a `.deb` and an `.rpm`
for Linux. The macOS app is not signed by Apple yet: the first time,
open it with right-click › Open, or allow it in System Settings › Privacy
& Security.

Installed, usta opens `usta://<forge link>` links, such as
`usta://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/1`, from anywhere on the
system. Once a day it checks for a newer release (Settings > Updates).

### With Nix

The flake has a Home Manager module, for macOS and Linux, and NixOS and
nix-darwin modules. On macOS they install `usta.app` (Home Manager links
it into `~/Applications/Home Manager Apps`), so `usta://` links and
notifications work.

```nix
{
  inputs.usta.url = "github:abdivasiyev/usta";

  # in a Home Manager configuration
  imports = [ inputs.usta.homeManagerModules.default ];
  programs.usta = {
    enable = true;
    settings = {
      interval = "5m";        # "1m", "2m", "5m", "15m" or "manual"
      theme = "dark";         # "system", "light" or "dark"
      notifications = true;
      onlyInBackground = false;
      openLinks = true;
      checkUpdates = false;
    };
  };
}
```

Each setting is optional. One that is set shows as "Set in Nix" in
usta's Settings and is not changed there; the rest stay yours. Home
Manager writes them to `~/.config/usta/config.json`.
`nixosModules.default` and `darwinModules.default` take the same
`programs.usta` options for every user, written to
`/etc/xdg/usta/config.json`; a user's own Home Manager settings win
over them. `overlays.default` adds `pkgs.usta`.

## Run

With [Nix](https://nixos.org) and flakes enabled:

```sh
nix run github:abdivasiyev/usta
```

## Build

Everything comes from the flake: GHC 9.12, GTK 4 and the Haskell
dependencies.

```sh
nix build        # the app, in ./result/bin/usta
nix develop      # a shell with GHC, cabal and haskell-language-server
```

Inside `nix develop`:

```sh
cabal build
cabal run usta
```

`cabal run usta -- <flag>` opens other screens, for working on them:

| Flag           | Opens                                    |
|----------------|------------------------------------------|
| `--gallery`    | every component on one page              |
| `--welcome`    | the first-run screen, before any account |
| `--first-sync` | the inbox while the first sync runs      |

## Release

`scripts/macos-app.sh` builds `dist/usta.app` and `dist/usta.dmg` with
every library inside, so they run without Nix; set `USTA_SIGN_IDENTITY`
to sign with a Developer ID. Pushing a tag `v<version>` that matches
`usta.cabal` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which builds both
downloads and attaches them to a new release; its header lists the
secrets for signing and notarizing.
